origin.description: Replace the first code point that belongs to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Text that replaces the first match. NA makes the string NA when a match exists.

origin.details: One code point is replaced. A miss returns the original string, even when the replacement is NA.
origin.example:
x <- stri_replace_first_charclass("ab12", "\\p{N}", "X")
sentence <- paste0('stri_replace_first_charclass("ab12", "\\p{N}", "X") returns ', x, '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Replace the first code point that belongs to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error. Membership is ICU 76, Unicode 16.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Text that replaces the first match. NA makes the string NA when a match exists.

translation.details: One code point is replaced. A miss returns the original string, even when the replacement is NA.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_replace_first_charclass
x = stri_replace_first_charclass("ab12", "\\p{N}", "X")
sentence = f'stri_replace_first_charclass("ab12", "\\p{{N}}", "X") returns {x[0]}.'
print(sentence)
